chunks: And from him, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, and others, regarding the names of the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), their lineages, and their descriptions.

Ayesha, and Hafsa, and Umm Habeeb bint Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and Zaynab bint Jahsh, and Sawda bint Zam'a, and Maymuna bint al-Harith, and Safiyya bint Hayy ibn Akhtab, and Umm Salama bint Abu Umayya, and Juwayriya bint al-Harith.

And Ayesha was from Taym, and Hafsa was from Adi, and Umm Salama was from Banu Makhzum, and Sawda was from Banu Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza, and Zaynab bint Jahsh was from Banu Asad; and a number of them were from Banu Umayya, and Umm Habib bint Abu Sufyan was from Banu Umayya, and Maymuna bint al-Harith was from Banu Hilal, and Safiyya bint Hayy ibn Akhtab was from Banu Israel.

And he (peace be upon him and his family) passed away with nine wives, and besides these were those who had gifted themselves to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and Khadeeja bint Khuwaylid, the mother of his child, and Zaynab bint Abi al-Jawn who was deceived, and al-Kindiya.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not marry (another wife) upon Khadeeja.

key_terms.لَمْ يَتَزَوَّجْ عَلَى: Did not marry upon (while she was alive)

ai.seo_question: Who were the wives of the Prophet Muhammad and what were their tribal lineages according to Shia sources?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi meticulously details the genealogical and tribal backgrounds of the Prophet’s wives, emphasizing their social status and lineage, which was crucial for understanding the political and social dynamics of early Islam. It distinguishes between the nine wives present at his death and other unique marital relationships, such as Khadija, while a supplementary report from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the Prophet did not contract a new marriage during Khadija’s lifetime, a point of scholarly discussion regarding the chronology of his marriages. This context highlights the Prophet’s marriages not merely as personal unions but as strategic alliances that reinforced tribal cohesion and social integration.
